exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Ordering at a Restaurant
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Are you ready to order, madam? What would you like today?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: I'm not sure. What would you recommend?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Right now our red braised pork is the most popular dish.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: That sounds good. But I don't eat much meat. Anything lighter?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Then you might like the hand-torn cabbage and the mushroom soup.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Perfect. I'll have both of those, please.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Of course. Would you like a sweet dessert at the end?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: No, thank you. I'm trying to cut down on sugar.

exercises.translation_cn: 服务员问女士点什么并推荐红烧肉;顾客不太吃肉,想要清淡些;服务员推荐手撕包菜和菌菇汤;顾客都要;问是否要甜点;顾客说在控糖,谢绝。

questions.stem: What does the waiter first recommend?
Why does the customer want something else?
options: She does not eat much meat.

questions.stem: Which two dishes does the customer finally choose?

options: She is trying to cut down on sugar.

options: She orders everything on the menu.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 The Eight Great Cuisines
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: China is a large country, and its food changes greatly from place to place.
People often speak of the eight great cuisines, each with its own character.
Sichuan food in the southwest is famous for its bold and spicy flavours.
Cantonese food in the south is lighter, and its dim sum is loved by many.
Wherever you go, food is used to show friendship and kindness to guests.
exercises.translation_cn: 中国地域辽阔,各地饮食差异很大;人们常说八大菜系,各有特色;西南的川菜以浓烈麻辣著称;南方的粤菜较清淡,点心广受喜爱;无论到哪里,食物都用来向客人表达友谊与善意。

questions.stem: How many great cuisines are mentioned?
What is Sichuan food famous for?
How is Cantonese food described?
Why does food differ across China?
options: Because the country is large and places differ.
Because there is only one cuisine.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 A Warm Welcome in Beijing
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: How was your first meal after you arrived in Beijing?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: It was unforgettable. We were tired and couldn't read the menu at all.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: So how did you manage to order?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: We didn't. The chef just smiled and chose the dishes for us.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: That was very kind of him. What did you taste?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: For the first time, I tried the Sichuan peppercorn. It tingled on my tongue.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Did you enjoy the meal?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: I did. But what I remember most is the friendship he offered us.

exercises.translation_cn: A 问 B 到北京后第一顿饭如何;B 说难忘,当时很累又看不懂菜单;A 问怎么点菜;B 说没点,厨师微笑着替他们选菜;A 说他真好心;B 第一次尝到四川花椒,舌尖发麻;最难忘的是厨师给予的友谊。

questions.stem: What problem did the speaker have at first?
options: He could not read the menu.

questions.stem: Who chose the dishes for them?
What did the speaker taste for the first time?
How did the peppercorn feel on his tongue?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 A Tip for Healthy Eating
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple tip for anyone who wants to eat in a healthier way.
Try to cut down on sweet drinks and desserts, which are full of sugar.
Fill your plate instead with fresh fruit and vegetables.
It is also a good idea to eat slowly and chew your food well.
Remember, a balanced diet in moderation is the real key to good health.
exercises.translation_cn: 给想吃得更健康的人一个小贴士:尽量少喝含糖的甜饮料、少吃甜点;多用新鲜水果和蔬菜装盘;吃慢点、嚼细些也是个好主意;记住,适度均衡的饮食才是健康的真正关键。

questions.stem: Who is this tip for?
options: Anyone who wants to eat in a healthier way.

questions.stem: What should you cut down on?
What should you put on your plate instead?
What does the speaker say about eating?
options: Eat as fast as you can.

questions.stem: What is described as the real key to good health?
options: Eating a huge meal once a day.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Asking the Chef for Advice
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Chef, my soup never tastes as good as yours. What am I doing wrong?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Tell me, do you boil the bones for long enough?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Maybe not. I usually cook it for only twenty minutes.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: That's the problem. Good soup needs slow cooking over low heat.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: I see. Anything else I should try?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Yes. Add just a little vinegar at the end. It brings out the flavour.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Thank you so much. I'll try both tricks tonight.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Good luck. Remember, patience is the real secret of cooking.

exercises.translation_cn: A 向厨师请教:汤总不如他的好喝,哪里出错;厨师问骨头炖得够不够久;A 只煮二十分钟;厨师说要小火慢炖;A 还要注意什么;厨师建议最后加一点醋提味;A 道谢说今晚都试;厨师说耐心才是做菜真正的秘诀。

questions.stem: What is the speaker's problem?
options: His soup is not as tasty as the chef's.

questions.stem: What does the chef say about cooking the bones?
options: They need slow cooking over low heat.

questions.stem: What should the speaker add at the end?

What does the chef call the real secret of cooking?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Why Eating Slowly Helps
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Have you ever wondered why eating slowly is good for you?
It takes about twenty minutes for your brain to know that you are full.
People who eat too quickly often end up eating more than they need.
Eating slowly also helps your body digest the food better.
So next time, put down your chopsticks and enjoy every single bite.
exercises.translation_cn: 你想过为什么吃得慢对身体好吗?大脑大约要二十分钟才知道你饱了;吃得太快的人往往吃得超过所需;慢慢吃还能帮助身体更好地消化;所以下次放下筷子,好好享受每一口。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why eating slowly is good for you.

questions.stem: How long does the brain take to know you are full?
